notesStmt.note: On the verso of this manuscript is a letter addressed to Whitman, dated 19 June 1889. Based on the date of this incoming letter and the date "Some Personal and Old–Age Jottings" was first published, this manuscript must have been composed between 1889–1891.

This manuscript contains a draft of a portion of "Some Personal and Old-Age Jottings," an essay first published in the March 1891 issue of Lippincott's Magazine under the title, "Some Personal and Old-Age Memoranda." It was then included, largely unchanged, in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

On the verso is a letter to Whitman, dated 19 June 1889. The signature of this letter has been obscured by a scrap of paper, which appears to have been pasted to this surface.

body.p: The Had been simmering within inside for six or seven years—broke out ‸during those at times ‸temporarily and then recuperated went over. But now a serious attack, beyond all cure. Dr. D., my Washington physician, ‸(and a good one, to whom I pay respect and faith yet) said it was from ‸the result of too extreme bodily and emotional strain ‸continued at Washington and 'down in front' in 18612, '63, '4, and '5, But The I doubt if ever a heartier, stronger healthier physique ever lived from 1840 to '70. My greatest call (Quaker) to go around & do all what I could among the ‸suffering sick and wounded was that I seem'd to be so well. I considered myself invulnerable
